faqs.q: Do I need a permit for modified bitumen roofing in East Orange?

runs.v: On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, repairing or replacing more than 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. A detached one- or two-family reroof counts as ordinary maintenance and requires no permit. Permits go through the East Orange Building Division at City Hall, 44 City Hall Plaza.

faqs.q: Is torch-applied modified bitumen safe on an occupied East Orange apartment building?

runs.v: Yes, with precautions: torch work follows NRCA hot-work protocol with extinguishers and a fire watch, and on an occupied walk-up Newark Quality Roofing applies self-adhered SBS or cold-adhesive modified bitumen with no open flame at the roof.

faqs.q: What is the difference between SBS and APP modified bitumen?

runs.v: SBS stays flexible in cold weather, while APP runs heat-resistant and UV-stable but stiffer in cold, per ARMA modified-bitumen guidance. Newark Quality Roofing installs SBS for the Essex County freeze-thaw climate.

faqs.q: How long does a modified bitumen roof last on an East Orange building?

runs.v: Modified bitumen lasts 20 years on average, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, against EPDM at 15 to 25 years and TPO at 7 to 20 years. Seam and flashing maintenance carries it toward the upper end.
